data.narrative:
Synchron is a Series D biotech company that has raised over $200M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in Biotech & Health, with particular relevance from same-stage companies including Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B Series C), Chai Discovery ($3.8B Series C), and New Limit ($3.1B Series C).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical of Series D advancement to the $200M total raised proxy, implying a $300M valuation. Peer-median analysis across the 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a $3.8B median valuation, with a range of $3.1B to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales (median 6.2x across the 3 public tickers) cannot be applied due to absence of revenue disclosure for the target.

The two applicable methods produce a wide range: $255M (lower bound from stage-progression) to $4.4B (upper bound from peer dispersion). The median across both methods is $2.0B. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median reflects the high variance in late-stage biotech valuations; the peer set includes Colossal at $10.3B versus New Limit at $3.1B, both at similar stages. Key uncertainties include revenue scale, clinical-stage maturity, and capital efficiency relative to named peers. The analysis suggests a $2.0B–$3.8B range as most defensible given peer clustering.
